PullRequest.Title: Pause automatic inline completions on metered connections
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Respect metered connections in the existing network-backed inline completion providers owned by the codebase, without adding a generic provider API.

- skip new automatic Copilot ghost-text requests while the connection is metered
- skip new automatic Copilot next-edit suggestion (NES) requests while the connection is metered, including requests triggered by switching editors
- preserve explicit user-triggered requests and requests already in flight
- leave local-only providers such as Emmet unchanged

## Issue coverage

- Fixes #297407: automatic Copilot completions no longer start network requests on metered connections.
- Fixes #297412: editor switches can trigger NES refreshes, but those automatic provider requests now stop before request logging or network work when the connection is metered.

Third-party providers and non-completion network activity are intentionally outside this change.

## Validation

- `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`
- `npm run compile`

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic Copilot ghost-text request while the connection is metered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor invokes CopilotInlineCompletionItemProvider.provideInlineCompletionItems; the added trigger-kind and cached env-state check completes before logging, prompt construction, cache lookup, or backend access, so only the local check remains on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Streams a Copilot completion when no usable local completion exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, a cold automatic invocation could create one logical completion backend request; warm cache or async-request reuse could avoid it. After the diff, metered automatic invocations create zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Metered status did not affect provider entry, so automatic requests continued through existing cache and network logic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before the diff, a cold response could gate suggestion production; after the diff this boundary is not reached and the provider returns immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reads metered status already mirrored into the extension host; status initialization and changes are forwarded separately by MainThreadMeteredConnection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The changed provider performs one local cached boolean read per automatic invocation; there is no per-invocation IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider did not read metered status; the underlying status-propagation service already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant-time local read before all expensive provider work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automatic editor completion triggers, commonly scaling with typing events; each metered invocation now does one constant-time gate and no backend request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One ghost-text provider invocation per editor request. Under the regular joint provider it can be invoked alongside NES, but both added metered gates resolve immediately; no new queue, limiter, or network concurrency is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new gate is before ghost-text cache lookup, so both cold and warm automatic invocations return immediately while metered. Existing cache keys, async request reuse, and negative behavior are unchanged when unmetered.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line is the first statement in the provider, and env.isMeteredConnection resolves from an extension-host boolean field rather than synchronous IPC.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact automatic trigger frequency and cache-hit rate vary with typing and editor configuration, but the changed path strictly removes downstream work on metered connections.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes prompt/cache/network work from this metered automatic path and adds only a local cached-state read.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic next-edit suggestion request while metered, including editor-switch refreshes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor or joint provider invokes InlineCompletionProviderImpl.provideInlineCompletionItems; the added check returns before CapturingToken/logger creation, workspace/model processing, diagnostics racing, cache lookup, serialization, and the stateless next-edit stream.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Builds and streams a Copilot next-edit request on cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, each effective cache miss could start or join one pending/speculative next-edit stream; repeated triggers may coalesce when state matches. After the diff, new metered automatic invocations start or join zero streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic metered invocations entered the normal cache/coalescing/network path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Before the diff, cache processing or a backend first edit could gate NES completion; after the diff the provider returns before that path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local boolean read per automatic NES provider invocation and no per-request IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No metered-state read occurred in the NES provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant-time local gate replaces all downstream request setup on the metered path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automatic NES triggers from edits, cursor/editor changes, and joint-provider refreshes; cost after the diff remains O(1) per metered trigger with zero new backend streams.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The regular joint provider may invoke NES and ghost text concurrently. Both now resolve without downstream work while metered. Existing pending/speculative request coalescing is bypassed for new automatic invocations, while already-running work is not canceled by the added gate.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The gate precedes NES cache and pending/speculative request lookup. Cold and warm new automatic requests are skipped while metered; existing in-flight requests remain governed by pre-existing cancellation/coalescing. Unmetered cache behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the early return is directly before request logging and the traced getNextEdit path, and the environment getter is local state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor-switch and typing trigger rates vary, and cache/coalescing previously reduced some backend calls; nevertheless the changed early return can only reduce work on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change removes local model work and cold network requests, and does not increase concurrency or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic Copilot completions while the connection is not metered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each provider evaluates trigger kind and the local metered boolean, then follows the same pre-diff logging, cache, model, and backend path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetches ghost text and/or streams NES on effective cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged by the diff: up to one logical invocation per selected provider per editor trigger, with the regular joint strategy potentially invoking both and existing caches/coalescing reducing actual backend calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider and network paths ran with the same cache keys, grouping, and concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged apart from one constant-time local state check before provider work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Typing/editor automatic-trigger frequency, with at most one added constant-time check in each provider actually invoked.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing behavior is retained: standalone strategies invoke one provider, while the regular joint strategy can race ghost text and NES; existing cancellation and pending/speculative coalescing remain intact.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold misses and warm hits use exactly the pre-existing ghost-text and NES cache/coalescing logic; the added false predicate neither changes keys nor invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source tracing shows the getter returns an in-memory field and no changed allocation, serialization, IPC, or I/O follows from the check itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of editor triggers and cache misses varies, but the only added unmetered cost is a boolean getter plus proposed-API enablement check per selected provider invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable regression. The added local check is negligible and does not amplify an expensive resource or boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly invoked Copilot ghost-text or NES request on any connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Because triggerKind is not Automatic, short-circuit evaluation bypasses env.isMeteredConnection and execution enters the exact pre-diff provider path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Performs an explicit completion or next-edit backend request when existing caches cannot satisfy it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly as before: selected providers may issue one logical request each on an effective miss, with existing joint concurrency and coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Explicit requests followed these same paths regardless of connection status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The same cache/model/network work remains on the explicit request critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit user invocations; the diff adds no per-invocation work after the first trigger-kind comparison already needed for the branch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged: explicit requests use the existing standalone or joint-provider strategy, cancellation, races, and request coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing warm-cache service and cold-request behavior are unchanged because the new conjunction short-circuits before reading metered state for explicit triggers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: JavaScript short-circuit semantics and both changed predicates make this path behaviorally and computationally unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Explicit request frequency and cache hit rates vary, but no changed mechanism executes for this trigger kind.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced provider registration, joint-provider concurrency, environment-state propagation, ghost-text cache/network behavior, and NES cache/coalescing/network behavior. The PR adds constant-time local gates that eliminate downstream work on metered automatic paths while leaving unmetered and explicit paths effectively unchanged; no performance finding or qualifying regression-fix record was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
